scope: Public-source reference provenance for the TH14 ETEX increment; references provide research leads. Original local executable execution supplies the native comparisons.

references.application: Used ETEX names, parameter roles, bounce wall masks, save/step mode descriptions and target-speed acceleration as leads for TH14 retail disassembly. TH16 mode 7 is not copied into TH14, whose dispatcher accepts only modes 0..6.
references.limit: Documentation targets TH16/17; it is not TH14 correctness evidence.

references.application: Reviewed existing bullet transform/motion separation and web-port architecture. Kept TH14 consumers isolated from the shared TH11/TH12 implementation. Also compared the inherited end-choice scheduler and HUD queue: its TH11 font/coordinates/formatting explain the prior TH14 mismatch. TH14 sidebar, five choices and manual behavior were separately recovered from TH14 retail execution. Reviewed TH11 player death/respawn and Bomb power consumption: these explain inherited TH14 lifecycle errors. TH14 hit/death effects, stock consumption, refill and laser-only first 30 respawn frames were recovered from TH14 retail instructions rather than copied across versions. HUD icon registration must follow TH14 manager-owned layer 24 rather than embedded TH11 VMs. Actual Bomb animation scripts and damage virtuals also differ; the shared TH11 Bomb controller remains a known incomplete path.
references.limit: Opcode numbering differs from TH14, including 0x40 and 0x200000; code cannot be copied by matching opcode number.

references.application: Reviewed the distinction between delinked executable recovery, compilable functions and byte-matching decompilation; retained executable execution as the proof boundary.
references.limit: Its README describes an incomplete decompilation. A buildable reference does not establish TH14 or browser equivalence.

references.application: Reviewed the TH14 archive/ANM tooling and supported-title table while tracing retail front.anm scripts and Bomb resource script differences.
references.limit: Resource formats and script inspection provide leads; neither the tool support table nor a decoded ANM establishes runtime, Bomb or pixel equivalence.
